title: Edge bound for Hamilton-connected graphs
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on $\nu \ge 4$ vertices with $\varepsilon$ edges. If $G$ is Hamilton-connected — that is, every two distinct vertices of $G$ are joined by a Hamilton path — then \[3\nu + 1 \le 2\varepsilon.\]
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite simple graph
the number of vertices satisfies nu >= 4
replaced:
Ex 4.2.11(a): a Hamilton-connected graph satisfies \texttt{3$\nu$ + 1 $\le$
2$\varepsilon$} (Moon).

\textbf{4.2.11} $G$ is \emph{Hamilton-connected} if every two vertices of $G$ are
connected by a Hamilton path. (a) Show that if $G$ is Hamilton-connected and $\nu \ge
4$, then $\varepsilon \ge [\frac{1}{2}(3\nu+1)]$.
